_note: v2 hook overrides for le Quai du Lavoir (ST_lavoir, S02_home), a sunny canal-side washing quay in spring, the second half of the daily-routine street (ST_routine seg005-009). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings): Monsieur Verbe the striped mime acts out each verb; the hand mirror marks the reflexive verbs.

fr_cirer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe rubs a black boot with WAX from his little tin until it shines: he POLISHES it, smooth as CERA (see-RAY).
fr_cirer_verb.why: Cire (wax, Latin cera) → cirer = to wax, to polish (il cire ses chaussures). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_gratter_verb.hook: Puzzled, Monsieur Verbe SCRATCHES his head like a cat at a GRATE (grah-TAY).
fr_gratter_verb.why: GRATE → gratter = to scratch, to scrape (le chat gratte à la porte); se gratter = to scratch oneself. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_detacher_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe unclips the beagle's lead from the bollard: he DETACHES it and the dog is free (day-tah-SHAY).
fr_detacher_verb.why: DETACH → détacher = to untie, to detach (détache le chien); also to remove a stain. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_nouer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe KNOTS the boat's rope round the mooring post: a NOOSE-like loop, NOW tied fast (noo-AY).
fr_nouer_verb.why: Un nœud (a knot) → nouer = to tie, to knot (il noue sa cravate). RED beret = regular -er. (je noue, nous nouons).

fr_clouer_verb.hook: Bang! Monsieur Verbe hammers a nail into the bench with a CLOU (nail) and his hammer: he NAILS it (kloo-AY).
fr_clouer_verb.why: Un clou (a nail, think CLOVE-shaped) → clouer = to nail (il cloue une planche); être cloué au lit = to be stuck in bed. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_voiler_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe drapes a cloth over the canary's cage like a VEIL: bedtime for the bird (vwah-LAY).
fr_voiler_verb.why: Un voile (a VEIL) → voiler = to veil, to cover (les nuages voilent le soleil). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_salir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe looks down at the mud SALLYING all over his stripes: he has got himself DIRTY, SULLIED (sah-LEER).
fr_salir_verb.why: SULLY, sale (dirty) → salir = to make dirty (ne salis pas ton pantalon !); se salir = to get dirty. GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous salissons).

fr_souiller_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe gasps: the muddy puppy SOILS the clean white sheet with paw prints (soo-YAY).
fr_souiller_verb.why: SOIL, SULLY → souiller = to soil, to stain, to defile (more literary than salir). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_blanchir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe lifts a sparkling shirt out of the suds, now BLANCHED snow-white (blahn-SHEER).
fr_blanchir_verb.why: BLANCH, blanc (white) → blanchir = to whiten, to bleach, to launder; also to turn white (ses cheveux blanchissent). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous blanchissons).

fr_eblouir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe shields his eyes: the shiny brass basin flashes so bright it DAZZLES him, like a BLUR of light (ay-bloo-EER).
fr_eblouir_verb.why: Éblouir = to dazzle (le soleil m'éblouit); éblouissant = dazzling. GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous éblouissons).

fr_masquer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe holds a carnival MASK over his face: he MASKS and hides it (mahs-KAY).
fr_masquer_verb.why: MASK → masquer = to mask, to hide (les arbres masquent la maison). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_repasser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe IRONS a shirt on the ironing board, PASSING the iron over it again and again: RE-PASS (ruh-pah-SAY).
fr_repasser_verb.why: Re + PASS → repasser = to iron (je repasse mes chemises); also to pass by again, to resit; un fer à repasser = an iron. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_dechainer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe pulls the CHAIN off the gate and the geese burst out honking: he UNCHAINS them, UNLEASHES them (day-sheh-NAY).
fr_dechainer_verb.why: Dé + CHAIN → déchaîner = to unleash, to whip up (ses mots ont déchaîné la colère); une chaîne = a chain. RED beret = regular -er. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (day-shay-NAY -> day-sheh-NAY).

fr_frotter_verb.hook: Brrr! Monsieur Verbe RUBS his hands together FRantically for warmth (froh-TAY).
fr_frotter_verb.why: Frotter = to rub, to scrub (frotte la casserole) ; se frotter les mains = to rub one's hands. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_tremper_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe dunks his croissant into the big bowl and lets it SOAK: TEMPERing it soft (trahn-PAY).
fr_tremper_verb.why: Tremper = to soak, to dip, to dunk (il trempe son croissant dans son chocolat); trempé = soaking wet. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_secher_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe pegs the dripping shirt on the line so the sun DRIES it, as dry as a SEC wine (say-SHAY).
fr_secher_verb.why: Sec / sèche (dry) → sécher = to dry (le linge sèche au soleil); informally, to skip a class. RED beret = regular -er. (je sèche, nous séchons).

fr_heriter_verb.hook: Beside Grandma's portrait, Monsieur Verbe opens her treasure chest: he has INHERITED her keepsakes, his HERITAGE (ay-ree-TAY).
fr_heriter_verb.why: HERITAGE, INHERIT → hériter (de) = to inherit (elle a hérité de la maison de sa grand-mère). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_revetir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe swirls a long blue cloak over his shoulders: he is RE-VESTED, dressed in it (ruh-vay-TEER).
fr_revetir_verb.why: VEST, VESTments → revêtir = to put on, to don, to cover (revêtir un uniforme; le mur est revêtu de bois). GOLD beret = irregular, like vêtir (je revêts, nous revêtons, revêtu).

fr_palir_verb.hook: A spider drops in front of Monsieur Verbe's nose and he goes PALE, PALLID, green with fright (pah-LEER).
fr_palir_verb.why: PALE, PALLID → pâlir = to turn pale, to fade (elle pâlit de peur). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous pâlissons).

fr_franchir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe leaps over the hurdle: he CLEARS it in one bound, a free FRANCHISE to cross (frahn-SHEER).
fr_franchir_verb.why: Franc (free) → franchir = to cross, to clear, to get over (franchir la frontière, franchir un obstacle). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous franchissons).

fr_defoncer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe bursts right through the paper hoop: he SMASHES IT IN, DE-FENCE (day-fohn-SAY).
fr_defoncer_verb.why: Dé + fond (bottom) → défoncer = to smash in, to break down (ils ont défoncé la porte); also to deep-plow. RED beret = regular -er. (nous défonçons).

fr_creuser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe DIGS a hole with his spade, deep as a CREVICE (kreuh-ZAY).
fr_creuser_verb.why: Creux (hollow) → creuser = to dig, to hollow out (le chien creuse un trou). RED beret = regular -er. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (kruh-ZAY -> kreuh-ZAY).

fr_masser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe MASSAGES the old gentleman's shoulders, and he beams (mah-SAY).
fr_masser_verb.why: MASSAGE → masser = to massage (il lui masse le dos); also to mass, to gather. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_essuyer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe WIPES the wet plate dry with his checked dish towel: ESSentially SWIPE it (ay-swee-YAY).
fr_essuyer_verb.why: Essuyer = to wipe, to dry (essuie la vaisselle, s'il te plaît); un essuie-glace = a windshield wiper. RED beret = regular -er. (j'essuie, nous essuyons).

fr_redresser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe holds both sides of the crooked picture and STRAIGHTENS it: he RE-DRESSES it into line (ruh-dreh-SAY).
fr_redresser_verb.why: Re + DRESS (line up, as soldiers dress ranks) → redresser = to straighten, to set upright (redresse le tableau); se redresser = to sit up straight. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_loger_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe holds up a birdhouse and the bluebird moves in: he LODGES it, gives it a home (loh-ZHAY).
fr_loger_verb.why: LODGE → loger = to house, to put up; to stay, to live (nous logeons chez des amis); le logement = housing. RED beret = regular -er. (nous logeons).

fr_embarrasser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe blushes bright pink over the spilt milk pitcher: how EMBARRASSING (ahn-bah-rah-SAY).
fr_embarrasser_verb.why: EMBARRASS → embarrasser = to embarrass; also to clutter, to get in the way (ces cartons m'embarrassent). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_aneantir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe clutches his head as the hailstorm flattens his lettuces: WIPED OUT, brought to NOTHING (ah-nay-ahn-TEER).
fr_aneantir_verb.why: Néant (nothingness) → anéantir = to wipe out, to destroy; to devastate someone (la nouvelle l'a anéanti). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous anéantissons).
fr_aneantir_verb.note: A strong word for destroying or crushing someone.
